summary: Grafton County NH summit tower; built 1910 with Timberland Owners funds; cab gone and structure modified; no longer in active service.

facts.status_note: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).
facts.agency: Federal lookout per White Mountain History; 1910 tower paid for by NH Timberland Owners Association

access.note: Trail access to the lookout, per White Mountain History

visit.trail_note: We could not confirm whether the platform can be climbed today

events.note: One of ten towers built that year; NH Timberland Owners Association paid for Carrigain
Forum recollection of a USFS steel tower; unverified
Forum recollection that the steel tower was removed and the platform built soon after; unverified

resolved_conflicts.explanation: White Mountain History calls the Carrigain lookout greatly modified and FFLA says its cab is gone. Both fit a structure that has been altered. No source we read dates the cab's removal.

sources.title: Fire Tower on Mount Carrigain
sources.publisher: New England & New York Backcountry & Hiking Forum

notes_for_editor: The 1910 build and Timberland Owners funding come from the NH Family Hikes history page, a secondary source. The NHDFL state PDF returned 403 to both fetch tools. The 1940-1981 steel tower dates and the platform age come only from VFTT forum posts and are flagged unverified in the story. The cab removal date is unknown. The record's kind and status_note are correct; agency is null in the record. Staffing is inferred from 'not in active service' in White Mountain History, which is undated.
